about.title: Orgue Vivant
about.intro: Orgue Vivant is a community initiative to keep organ music alive in downtown Lille. We organise free or low-cost concerts, open to everyone.
about.stMaurice: The grand organ of Saint-Maurice was built in 1877 by the Maison Delmotte of Tournai, housed in a carved oak case crafted in 1878 by Lille cabinetmaker Charles Buisine-Rigot. The instrument underwent a major reconstruction in 1961 by Jean Pascal, who refounded approximately 85% of the organ while preserving the original case. With 48 stops across three manuals and pedal, four Barker machines, and a window console with 12 programmable combinations, it offers an exceptionally rich tonal palette. Its pitch is set at 435 Hz in equal temperament.
about.stEtienne: The gallery organ of Saint-Étienne is one of the most precious instruments in northern France. Built in 1840 by Daublaine-Callinet — a partnership between Louis Callinet and André Marie Daublaine — it was profoundly reworked in 1886 by master builder Aristide Cavaillé-Coll, then again in 1901 by Charles Mutin. Listed as a historical monument since 1980, this 42-stop instrument across three manuals and pedal bears witness to the evolution of French Romantic organ building. With its Barker machine on the Grand-Orgue and a pitch of 440 Hz, it remains a remarkably expressive instrument.
about.mission: Make organ music accessible, support the next generation of organists, and showcase Lille's musical heritage.

privacy.intro:
The data controller is the association Orgue Vivant, 19 Parvis Saint-Maurice, 59800 Lille, France, reachable at contact{'@'}orguevivant.fr.

This page describes the personal data processed by orguevivant.fr, why, for how long, who has access to it, and your rights. It is written in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the French Data Protection Act.
privacy.purposes:
Contact form — name, email address and message. Purpose: answering your request. Legal basis: our legitimate interest in replying to people who write to us. The message is forwarded by email to the association.

Newsletter — email address, subscription and confirmation dates. Purpose: sending you concert dates, artists and festival news. Legal basis: your consent, given by a subscription you confirm from your mailbox. You can withdraw it at any time through the unsubscribe link in every email; your address is then deleted immediately.

Administration area — email address and password (stored encrypted) of the volunteers who publish the site's content. Legal basis: our legitimate interest in running the site.

Audience measurement — number of visits and pages viewed, measured by Vercel Web Analytics. No cookie or identifier is stored on your device; the data is aggregated and cannot track you across sites. No consent is therefore required.

Technical logs — IP address and requests, recorded by the host for the security and proper operation of the site.
privacy.transfers: The United Kingdom benefits from an adequacy decision of the European Commission. Processing carried out in the United States by Vercel and Resend is governed by the European Commission's standard contractual clauses, incorporated in their data processing agreements.
privacy.retention:
– Contact form messages: one year after the last exchange.
– Newsletter: until you unsubscribe. An unconfirmed subscription is deleted after thirty days.
– Administrator accounts: for the duration of the volunteer's role.
– Audience measurement: aggregated data, no individual identifier.
– Technical logs: a few days.
privacy.rights:
You have the right to access, rectify and erase your data, to restrict or object to its processing, to data portability, and to withdraw your consent to the newsletter at any time.

To exercise them, write to contact{'@'}orguevivant.fr; we reply within one month and may ask you to prove your identity.

If you believe your rights are not respected, you can lodge a complaint with the CNIL, the French data protection authority (www.cnil.fr).
